about: Emulate round 14 (2026-10-06 18:13 UTC, from the call records), emulate-runs/community-s6d: v5 P3 (u1) and v5 P8 (u2) alone, two calls each, raw outputs exact (balance 238,627 -> 238,337).
p3-emuA: I don’t know how much of our fear of the future is accurate. It’s possible that the development of artificial intelligence will allow people to drastically improve the quality of their lives, or that it will cause millions of people to lose their jobs, or that it will put itself between people and a lot of other things they interact with, or that Chantress Seba will finally get a couple of those applications to communes in the hills through the mail.
p3-emuB: I don’t know if it’s unfounded fear or not, but it’s not outside the realm of possibilities that AI will drastically improve some people’s lives, suck the life out of millions, and be in the way of everything we want to do, anyway. At least until the inevitable Chantress Seba commune applications start to flow in.
p8-emuA: Access to medical care is one of the trickiest connections to sort out. A community may prefer to provide as much natural care as possible, but what if someone in the community needs trauma surgery, antibiotics, dental care, obstetric care in an emergency, or some other specialized care? It is important to talk about how community members will have access to these kinds of services, what kinds of care will be ensured by the shared money of the community, what kinds of care might need to be accessed through outside sources of money (or insurance), and how to treat people who want to access different levels of care.
p8-emuB: Access to medical care is one of the trickiest areas to make connections in. Some communities feel comfortable providing primarily natural medical care, but then what if a community member needs trauma surgery, antibiotics, dental work, obstetric emergency care, or some other kind of specialist care? It’s very important to hash out how community members will access these kinds of services, what will be guaranteed through shared community funds, what might need to be obtained through external funds or insurance, and how community members who want to access these levels of care will be treated.
